text: 72/SPEC cited src/claude-settings.mjs:346 as the cause of the duplicated hook blocks. That line is the PERMISSIONS splice; the hook behaviour is spliceSettings at :254-317 turning on isAofEntry at :169-174, and the carry-through is :285. The SPEC's remedy (change the merge) would have been wrong: isAofEntry is deliberate and deleting an unmarked entry would also delete this repo's own guard-test-isolation hook. Species: a grep landed on a plausible line and the claim was written from the hit rather than from the function.

Three of 72/SPEC's six levers had gone stale in the 17 days between scheduling (2026-08-16) and architecture (2026-09-02), each closed or reduced by a DIFFERENT item that shipped in between: the QA Edit grant by chore 76, the observability classifier by 68/ADR-006, the doc budget by 70/ADR-007. Every number in the objective was still stated as live. The measured direction of drift was not uniform either: scripts/test.mjs went the OTHER way, 275,100 B to 349,485 B. A milestone SPEC written more than a sprint before its architecture pass needs a re-derivation step, not a re-read; three of six is not an outlier rate.

Two Blockers in my own ADRs, one species: I asserted a change to a file WITHOUT reading the controls that already pin that file. (1) ADR-004 said scripts/test.mjs gains an argv reader and an extracted loop, additively — but REG-MUT-11 in acd-loop-suite-registration.test.mjs digests every non-registration runner LINE (:302-305) and anchors four region cuts inside runSuite's body (:291-294), so neither change has a conforming implementation that leaves it green. I read the file I was changing and not the guard over it. (2) ADR-007 hung the worktree prepare step on addWorktree, one of four materialisation doors, and not the dominant one — a continuing item takes reuseWorktreeOnBranch (mesh-worker-execution.mjs:1615-1617), which materialises a fresh empty tree at a new path. I named the door I had already read at :1962 for the REMOVAL and assumed it was the creation door too. Both would have been caught by one habit: before writing an ADR that changes a file, run the guard census over that file (grep test/arch for its path) and enumerate its sibling entry points, rather than citing the one call site the previous investigation happened to surface.

Third amendment round on one milestone's ARCHITECTURE, and the pattern across all three is the same: I write an ADR asserting a change to a file, and the feasibility pass discovers the file is already pinned, already has siblings, or already costs something I did not measure. Round 2: REG-MUT-11 pins scripts/test.mjs; four worktree doors not one. Round 3: importing scripts/test.mjs to run ONE suite costs 3.4-6.5s and assembles 8,401 entries, so the headline lever had a 47x fixed-cost regression in its commonest case that no ADR had priced. The habit that would have caught all of it at round one: for every file an ADR proposes to change, before writing the clause, (a) grep test/arch for its path, (b) enumerate its sibling entry points, and (c) MEASURE the thing the ADR is claiming to make cheaper. I did (c) for the CLI boot path unprompted and it produced the milestone's best clause; I did not do it for the test runner, which is the milestone's actual subject.
